# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book teaches system dynamics twice over: with interactive models you can run in the browser, and with Python you can read, change and extend.

Every chapter goes with a module of the [LoopBricks app](https://waelrash1.github.io/loopbricks/#/learn). The app is where you build intuition: drag a slider, predict what a model will do, then watch it happen. The chapter is where you take the same model apart in code. Both run the same model files, and a test checks that they give the same numbers at every time step, so what you see in one is what you get in the other.

## How to use the chapters

Each chapter is a Jupyter notebook. Open it in Google Colab with the badge at its top and run the cells in order; the first cell installs the `loopbricks` package. On your own machine:

```
pip install "loopbricks @ git+https://github.com/waelrash1/loopbricks.git@main#subdirectory=python"
```

Try the exercises before opening the worked answers. Predicting first, even wrongly, is what makes the result stick.

## Sources

The ideas build on the system dynamics literature, from Forrester's founding work to Sterman's *Business Dynamics: Systems Thinking and Modeling for a Complex World* (McGraw-Hill, 2000), cited where it helps. Many models are our own implementations of the small reusable structures described in Jim Hines' *Molecules of Structure*, whose names they keep. The text, code and simulation engines are our own; no Vensim or Stella files or software are used. LoopBricks is not affiliated with or endorsed by Jim Hines, Ventana Systems or isee systems. Vensim is a trademark of Ventana Systems, Inc.; Stella is a trademark of isee systems, inc.
